results.title: The 7 Best Apps You Can Use As a WhatsApp Alternative
results.content: Telegram is a popular messaging app that offers voice, video, and text chat along with a mix of security options. Voice calls are automatically encrypted end-to-end, for example, and the app offers a secret chat mode in which your texts are also end-to-end encrypted, plus have a self-destruct timer. Routine texts aren't as secure, though. It's also one of the few apps that lets you lock the app itself, so if someone gets physical access to your phone, they still can't read your messages in Telegram. It's free for iPhone, Android, and even runs in a browser. [...] If you're looking for the strongest security in a WhatsApp alternative, Signal is probably what you need. The app leans hard into privacy with complete end-to-end encryption for voice, video, and text conversations when you chat with other Signal users. And the company behind Signal is a US-based non-profit organization that has no profit incentive to sell your data. You can set messages to self-destruct as well. On the other hand, the app is missing a sense of fun you might be looking for; there are no stickers or built-in GIFs, for example. It's available for free for both iPhone and Android. [...] Kik is a little more than just a messaging app; it has a social component that makes it easy to meet new people to chat with, if you're looking for more than just a way to stay in touch with friends and family. Sort of like TikTok, you can join live broadcasts and watch and chat with a large number of other users. And when it comes to getting friends and family online, you can let people scan a QR code found in your profile to get them into a chat instantly. It's free for iPhone and Android, though there are a fair number of ads to contend with. If you value your privacy though, you can sign up with an email address without revealing your phone number.

results.title: Best WhatsApp Alternative for Business
results.content:
### Are there good alternatives to WhatsApp?

Yes. Signal for privacy, Telegram for communities/channels, iMessage for Apple users, Messenger/Instagram for social circles, and Lark for workplace collaboration with chat, docs, meetings, and workflows in one platform.

### Who is WhatsApp's biggest competitor?

Telegram is probably WhatsApp's biggest global messaging competitor, especially for large groups, channels, and communities. Telegram says it has over 1 billion active users and supports groups of up to 200,000 members. In the US, iMessage is the strongest everyday alternative. For workplace use, Lark is a stronger alternative to WhatsApp.

### Which app is safer than WhatsApp? [...] ### Which app is safer than WhatsApp?

For personal privacy, Signal is usually the safest choice because messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted by default, and Signal says it does not sell, rent, or monetize user data. Telegram is not safer by default because end-to-end encryption mainly applies to Secret Chats, not regular cloud chats. For enterprise teams, Lark is a strong option as a secure WhatsApp alternative. It offers business-ready admin controls, permission settings, and centralized workspace management, helping companies keep work communication more organized and better governed.

### Why do companies need a WhatsApp alternative for business? [...] ### What is the best WhatsApp Business alternative?

For teams that need internal collaboration, customer follow-ups, approvals, and project coordination, Lark can be a better WhatsApp Business alternative. It helps businesses organize conversations, documents, meetings, and workflows in one place instead of relying on scattered chat groups.

### Why choose Lark as a WhatsApp alternative app?

Lark is more than a WhatsApp alternative app. It is an all-in-one collaboration platform where teams can chat, co-edit documents, schedule meetings, manage tasks, and automate workflows. This makes it easier to keep business communication clear and actionable.

A big part of this popularity is the widespread perception that Telegram is highly secure, a perception only heightened by a number of governments, notably Indonesia, Russia, and Iran, trying to block or ban the app. [...] The other apps discussed above all offer useful features that will appeal to those who need them, whether it’s anonymous signup, business collaboration tools, or server federation. Element/Matrix is a particularly strong choice for privacy enthusiasts, although its niche user base severely hampers its practicality as a WhatsApp replacement. Olvid is also notable for the care it takes to minimize metadata and end-to-end authentication (albeit at the cost of easy contact discovery). [...] An alternative for secure communication is end-to-end encrypted email(new window). Proton Mail is based in Switzerland and open source. And with Proton Mail’s Password-protected Emails, you don’t need your recipient to use the same messenger service to benefit from end-to-end encryption. You can send end-to-end encrypted messages to anyone who has an email address.

As you take back your privacy in the digital age, anything you do to move more of your personal data behind strong encryption is an important step toward building an internet that puts people first.

## Not recommended

We don’t recommend Telegram, another open-source WhatsApp alternative, but you should know its pros and cons to understand why it is so popular, despite its shortcomings.
